title: Committee of Supply – Head N (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head N (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)

sections.label: Budget cut for Head N
sections.summary: A motion is moved to reduce the total sum allocated for Head N of the Estimates by $100.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I seek to move, “That the total sum to be allocated for Head N of the Estimates be reduced by $100”.

sections.label: Small states navigating giants
sections.summary: For small states like Singapore, the eternal test is to navigate safely between giants rather than overpower them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For small states like Singapore, this remains the eternal test – not to overpower giants but to navigate safely between them.

sections.label: Sovereignty and Russia's invasion
sections.summary: Russia's invasion of Ukraine is a grave breach of the UN Charter, and for a small state sovereignty is lifeblood, legitimacy and survival.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: On sovereignty, Russia's invasion of Ukraine remains a grave breach of the UN Charter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For a small state, sovereignty is our lifeblood, our legitimacy, our survival.

sections.label: Strains on global commerce
sections.summary: Rising tariffs, expanding industrial policies and strains within the WTO weaken global commerce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Rising tariffs, expanding industrial policies and strains within the World Trade Organization's (WTO's) weaken global commerce.

sections.label: Holding course like Odysseus
sections.summary: Like Odysseus, Singapore must be firm in principle, pragmatic in execution, steady in diplomacy, agile in adaptation and united to defend sovereignty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: He survived because he understood the dangers, disciplined the crew and held the course.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We must be firm in principle, pragmatic in execution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We must be steady in diplomacy, agile in adaptation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We must be united as a people to defend our sovereignty and we must ensure that the power of the law prevails over the law of power.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Like Odysseus steering between Scylla and Charybdis, we cannot eliminate every danger.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: But with judgment in strategy, discipline in execution and unity in purpose, we can hold our course, and we will emerge stronger on the other side.

sections.label: Post-Cold War assumptions challenged
sections.summary: The central challenge is that assumptions underpinning the post-Cold War order, such as open markets and compliance with international law, can no longer be taken for granted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The central challenge before us is this: the assumptions that underpinned the post-Cold War order, such as open markets and compliance with international law, can no longer be taken for granted.

sections.label: Singapore foreign policy principles
sections.summary: Singapore's foreign policy is anchored in the principles of sovereignty and the rule of law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singapore's foreign policy is anchored in the principles of sovereignty and the rule of law.

sections.label: Free trade and globalisation
sections.summary: On free trade, globalisation must be recognised as entering a more fragmented phase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Second, in relation to free trade, we must recognise that globalisation is entering a more fragmented phase.

sections.label: ASEAN cohesion and challenges
sections.summary: A cohesive ASEAN gives Southeast Asia collective weight, but ASEAN faces challenges from Myanmar's limited participation and the Thailand-Cambodia war.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: A cohesive and credible ASEAN provides Southeast Asia with collective weight and agency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, ASEAN is facing its own challenges, with Myanmar's participation limited by its political problems and the war between Thailand and Cambodia marking the first military confrontation between two ASEAN countries.

sections.label: Singapore-Johor corridor and Malaysia ties
sections.summary: The Singapore-Johor corridor is the fastest pathway to practical results, with opportunities to deepen ties with other Peninsular and East Malaysian cities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Singapore-Johor corridor is the fastest pathway to practical results, addressing our constraints in manpower, cost and energy resilience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Beyond Johor, there are opportunities to deepen ties with cities in the rest of Peninsular Malaysia as well as East Malaysian cities, such as Kuching and Kota Kinabalu, where complementarities in energy, food systems and digital sectors offer mutual economic benefits.

sections.label: Scaling trusted node status
sections.summary: Beyond immediate borders, trusted node status must be scaled across ASEAN, Australia and New Zealand, Northeast Asia, China and India.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Beyond our immediate borders, we must scale our trusted node status across ASEAN, Australia and New Zealand (ANZ), Northeast Asia, China and India.

sections.label: MFA plans for ASEAN chairmanship
sections.summary: The question asks how MFA plans to deepen regional cooperation and encourage ASEAN to move as a cohesive grouping during next year's chairmanship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: How is MFA planning to deepen regional cooperation, integration and encourage ASEAN to move together as a cohesive economic and political grouping during our chairmanship next year?

sections.label: Overseas missions and ambassador gaps
sections.summary: Overseas missions promote Singapore's interests, safeguard Singaporeans abroad and act as listening posts, but there are no resident ambassadors in Italy, Sweden, Canada, Brazil and Nigeria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Overseas missions serve as important frontlines in promoting Singapore's interests and safeguarding the well-being of Singaporeans abroad, as well as listening posts to understand what is really happening.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We currently lack resident ambassadors in Italy, Sweden, Canada, Brazil and Nigeria.

sections.label: Principles, international law, SAF deterrence
sections.summary: Singapore does not choose sides but principles, upholding international law, freedom of navigation and ASEAN centrality, while investing in the SAF and Home Team to deter aggression.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Our approach must remain clear and consistent: we do not choose sides, but we choose principles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: We uphold international law, freedom of navigation and ASEAN centrality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: At the same time, we must continue to invest in a strong and credible SAF and Home Team to deter aggression and safeguard our sovereignty.

sections.label: Championing open markets and cooperation
sections.summary: Singapore must continue to champion open markets, plurilateral agreements and cooperation among like-minded countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Singapore must continue to champion open markets, plurilateral agreements, and cooperation among like-minded countries.

sections.label: Technology as foreign policy soft power
sections.summary: The question asks whether MFA would consider technology a strategic tool in foreign policy to upgrade and push as soft power.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Would MFA consider technology as a strategic tool in our foreign policy that we upgrade and push as a soft power?

sections.label: US-China competition reshaping supply chains
sections.summary: US-China strategic competition is deepening and global supply chains are being reshaped by security concerns, export controls and geopolitical alignment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, US-China strategic competition is deepening and global supply chains are being reshaped by security concerns, export controls and geopolitical alignment.

sections.label: US-China evolution and Singapore's choices
sections.summary: The question asks how MFA sees the US-China relationship evolving and what it means for Singapore's ability to make its own choices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: On our strategic posture, how does MFA see the US-China relationship evolving, and what does it mean for Singapore’s ability to make our own choices?

sections.label: Resilience, US-China split, supply chains
sections.summary: MFA is asked how it works with MTI on geopolitical chokepoints, US-China technology split exposure, and positioning Singapore as a trusted hub.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Given that the world is shifting from efficiency to resilience, how is MFA working with the Ministry of Trade and Industry to make sure Singapore is not overly exposed to any single geopolitical chokepoint?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: How vulnerable are we to the US-China technology split, especially in semiconductors, AI and digital infrastructure that our companies rely on to stay competitive and families depend on for daily life?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: And as global supply chains re-organise, how are we positioning Singapore as a trusted, stable hub so that businesses continue to choose Singapore, create good jobs and keep our economy strong?

sections.label: Singaporeans' visa-free access to 192 countries
sections.summary: Singaporeans have visa-free access to 192 countries, signifying strong diplomatic ties, stability and international reputation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Singaporeans are privileged with visa-free access to 192 countries, signifying strong diplomatic ties, exceptional stability and good reputation internationally.

sections.label: Public understanding of foreign policy principles
sections.summary: MFA is asked how it will strengthen public understanding of Singapore's foreign policy principles to sustain domestic support in polarising situations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: How will MFA enhance efforts to strengthen public understanding of Singapore's foreign policy principles so that there is sustained domestic support for the stand we take in complex and polarising situations?

sections.label: Community organisations rebuilding Gaza
sections.summary: Community organisations expressed interest in rebuilding Gaza, and MFA is urged to engage and collaborate with non-governmental organisations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Plus, many community organisations I met at a dialogue after the working visits also shared their interest in playing a part to rebuild Gaza.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: I urge MFA to be intentional in engaging and collaborating with our homegrown and international non-governmental organisations, so more Singaporeans can participate in the Ministry's efforts to do its part in helping the ones in need.

sections.label: Multilateral processes and new institutions
sections.summary: MFA is asked how it balances commitment to new institutions like the Board of Peace with assessing and possibly pivoting when they no longer function as intended.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Yet, multilateral processes today are increasingly constrained by declining consensus and major contributors reassessing engagement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: So, in such an environment, how does MFA balance continued commitment to establish on new institutions, such as the Board of Peace, with the need to assess and possibly pivot when these institutions no longer function as intended?

sections.label: Prioritising partnerships as influence disperses
sections.summary: MFA is asked how it determines which partnerships to prioritise as influence becomes more dispersed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: As influence becomes more dispersed, how is MFA determining which partnerships to prioritise?

sections.label: Students learning and Singapore openness
sections.summary: Students learning languages and interacting with other societies helps them understand why Singapore must stay open and outward-looking.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: And our students pick up new languages, travel and interact with people from different societies, they learn.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: And when they understand the world better, they will also understand why Singapore must remain open, outward-looking and engage at the global stage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: But its impact can also be deeply personal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: We must ensure that our diplomacy and our people are ready for that reality.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: We must continue investing and strengthening our appreciation at home, building partnerships abroad and staying principal in uncertain times.

sections.label: MFA engagement and grassroots training
sections.summary: MFA has stepped up dialogues and workshops, and should work with the People's Association to train grassroots leaders as a front line of resilience.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: MFA has already been stepping up engagements with students, youths, businesses and community groups through dialogues and workshops to explain our operating context and foreign policy in accessible terms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We should build on this by working more closely with the People's Association (PA) to train grassroots leaders as well as other community leaders as a front line of resilience.

sections.label: Explainer materials and rapid-response lines
sections.summary: MFA should develop simple explainer materials and rapid-response lines so organisations can anchor discussions on facts rather than rumours during crises.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: MFA should also develop simple, shareable explainer materials and rapid‑response lines to clarify our positions quickly when major international crises break, so that grassroots leaders, schools, unions, businesses, religious and community organisations can anchor discussions on facts rather than rumours.

sections.label: Geopolitical literacy in curriculum
sections.summary: MFA has held about 150 dialogue sessions since January 2024, and should work with MOE to embed geopolitical literacy from secondary school onward.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Since January 2024, it has conducted some 150 dialogue sessions and workshops with students, youths and businesses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Building literacy requires the same cumulative approach that we apply to other 21st century core competencies, layered across years, integrated into multiple disciplines and reinforced over time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I urge MFA to work more deeply with the Ministry of Education (MOE) to embed geopolitical literacy throughout the curriculum from secondary school onward.

sections.label: Reviews and foreign policy decisions
sections.summary: Reviews are relevant, but strategic decisions should not become public referendums or be pressured by public sentiment, which would compromise foreign policy space.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: These reviews are relevant and it is important that the Government has its pulse on the ground.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, it will be unwise to turn strategic decisions of such a nature into public referendums, or for the Government to be pressured into taking certain decisions based on public sentiment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This will compromise the deafness and manoeuvrability and confine the space of our foreign policies which are critical in this complex geopolitical environment.

sections.label: Contested geopolitical environment
sections.summary: Singapore will have to navigate a more contested geopolitical environment for the foreseeable future, including intensifying US-China rivalry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Singapore will have to navigate a more contested geopolitical environment for the foreseeable future, including intensifying US-China rivalry.

sections.label: Open trade partners
sections.summary: For a small, open economy like Singapore, this is an existential challenge, and partners like the EU, Japan and South Korea share its commitment to open trade, multilateral rules and a stable international order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: For a small, open economy like Singapore, this is an existential challenge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Partners like the European Union (EU), Japan and South Korea share our commitment to open trade, multilateral rules and a stable international order.

sections.label: ASEAN centrality for Singapore
sections.summary: For Singapore, ASEAN remains central to its security and continued relevance, as Singapore assumes the ASEAN chairmanship amid growing global tensions.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For Singapore, ASEAN remains central to our security and continued relevance in the world.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This milestone comes at a particularly consequential moment as Singapore assumes the ASEAN chairmanship amid growing global tensions.

sections.label: ASEAN digital and power initiatives
sections.summary: Initiatives such as the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement and the ASEAN Power Grid are practical pathways to strengthen regional resilience, connectivity and competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Initiatives such as the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement and the ASEAN Power Grid are not abstract long-term ambitions but practical pathways to strengthen regional resilience, connectivity and competitiveness.

sections.label: Singapore chairmanship questions and diplomacy
sections.summary: Questions are raised on how Singapore will use its chairmanship to strengthen ASEAN cohesion and strategic autonomy and on outcomes for the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement, noting Singapore's diplomacy affects national security, international standing and overseas development space for enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: First, as ASEAN navigates a more contested geopolitical environment, how does Singapore intend to use its chairmanship to strengthen ASEAN cohesion and strategic autonomy so that the region remains united and not pulled apart by major-power competition?

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Second, as economic integration becomes increasingly digital, what concrete outcomes or milestones can we expect under Singapore's chairmanship for the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement?

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In particular, how is Singapore supporting efforts to narrow digital capability gaps among member states so that integration benefits the region as a whole?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Currently, international situation is complex, competition between countries intense, supply chain adjusting, rules and standards are also changing everywhere.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Therefore, Singapore's diplomacy not only relates to national security and our international standing, but also directly affects the overseas development space for Singapore enterprises.

sections.label: ASEAN trade and digital agreements
sections.summary: The signing of the upgrade to the ASEAN Trade in Goods Agreement will improve market access, transparency and connectivity for Singapore companies, and the substantive conclusion of the Digital Economy Framework Agreement is another milestone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The signing of the upgrade to the ASEAN Trade in Goods Agreement will improve market access, transparency and connectivity for Singapore companies doing business in the region.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The substantive conclusion of the Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA) is yet another milestone.

sections.label: ASEAN relevance and Singapore chairmanship
sections.summary: The Minister is asked about ASEAN's continued relevance and importance to Singapore and the region and Singapore's role in strengthening ASEAN integration as it takes on the ASEAN chairmanship in 2027.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: As we see ASEAN taking proactive steps to establish itself as a noteworthy regional platform, can the Minister share more on the continued relevance and importance of ASEAN to Singapore and the region as a whole and Singapore's role in the efforts to strengthen ASEAN integration, particularly as Singapore takes on the ASEAN chairmanship in 2027?

sections.label: Replicating ASEAN diplomatic framework elsewhere
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the cohesive diplomatic framework can be replicated in regions besides ASEAN.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Are there other regions besides ASEAN where we can replicate this cohesive diplomatic framework with?

sections.label: ASEAN unity and external powers
sections.summary: The passage states ASEAN is most effective when members act collectively, and divisions weaken its voice while external powers shape the regional agenda.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: ASEAN has always been most effective when member states act collectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: If we allow divisions to widen, ASEAN's voice will weaken and external powers will shape the regional agenda instead.

sections.label: Singapore ASEAN chairmanship 2027 priorities
sections.summary: The passage asks how MFA is prioritising ASEAN unity, economic integration, supply chain resilience and centrality ahead of Singapore's 2027 chairmanship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: As we prepare for Singapore's ASEAN chairmanship in 2027, how is MFA prioritising efforts to strengthen ASEAN unity and effectiveness so that ASEAN countries can continue to matter to both its members and to external partners?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In particular, how is the Ministry advancing economic integration, supply chain resilience and ASEAN centrality in a more fragmented global system?

sections.label: Gaza Board of Peace pledges
sections.summary: The passage states Board of Peace member countries pledged billions for Gaza, and only the US among permanent UN Security Council members joined the plan.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: On Gaza, for example, member countries of the Board of Peace have pledged billions, billions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Save for the US, no other permanent member of the UN Security Council has come on board this plan.

sections.label: Singapore support for Palestinians
sections.summary: The passage states MFA hosted Palestinian Authority Minister Estephan Salameh, Singapore contributed over $25 million in humanitarian aid, and asks Singapore's forward plan.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In recent days, MFA hosted Palestinian Authority's Minister of Finance and Planning Estephan Salameh to reaffirm our commitment that Singapore stands in support and solidarity of the Palestinians in capacity building and toward statehood.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In fact, we have already contributed more than $25 million in humanitarian aid of this crisis.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To the Ministry, I ask, what is Singapore's forward plan and contribution to alleviating this crisis and tragedy and what more can Singaporeans do in support of these efforts?

sections.label: New embassies as economic enablers
sections.summary: The passage states MFA is opening embassies in Mexico City and Addis Ababa, and Missions in emerging regions should be resourced as active economic enablers with MTI.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: MFA has already started to move in this direction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: We are opening new embassies in Mexico City and Addis Ababa, to serve as gateways to Latin America and East Africa and to deepen our understanding of these fast‑growing regions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: Our new and existing Missions in emerging regions should be resourced not just for diplomatic presence or administrative protocol, but as active economic enablers, working in tandem with the Ministry of Trade and Industry in mapping sectoral opportunities, curating pipelines of projects and matching them with Singapore companies, workers and researchers.

sections.label: Scholarships and internships in emerging regions
sections.summary: This passage states that AI cannot easily replace certain work and calls for expanding scholarships, internships and mid-career attachments in emerging regions, including sustainability and digital services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: This is the reality of how the world works that we cannot change and it is also something that AI is not able to easily replace.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: We can expand scholarships, internships and mid‑career attachments in emerging regions, especially in sectors where our capabilities align with their needs, including sustainability and digital services.

sections.label: 24-hour consular assistance for Singaporeans
sections.summary: This passage describes Singapore's duty officer response for Singaporeans in distress overseas, including assistance to over 800 during Hat Yai floods, and notes limits where no resident embassy exists.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: Even in the middle of the night, when a Singaporean encounters distress thousands of kilometres away, there is always a duty officer in Singapore ready to respond, coordinating assistance with MFA's overseas Missions, liaising with local authorities and supporting both the individual abroad and their families back home.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: This commitment was demonstrated during the recent floods in Hat Yai, where hundreds of Singaporeans were affected and more than 800 were safely assisted to return home through coordinated evacuation efforts.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: While the 24-hour hotline provides vital coordination and guidance, situations on the ground may sometimes require physical, in-person assistance, particularly in countries where Singapore does not maintain a resident embassy or consulate.

sections.label: End of post-war international order
sections.summary: This passage states the post-World War II international order was unique and has ended, and lists its former principles including multilateralism, international law, free markets and global institutions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The post-World War II international order actually is historically an unprecedented phase in global history and generally, the last 80 years have been a period of unprecedented peace and prosperity for most countries in the world, but the point is that it was unique.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: And the deeper point today is that that international order has ended.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: This order used to be characterised by principles of multilateralism, international law, sovereign equality, free markets, global supply chains organised on the basis of efficiency and global institutions – the UN, the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the World Bank, the WTO.

sections.label: Fragmentation and weaponisation of interdependence
sections.summary: This passage states that economic integration has given way to fragmentation and weaponisation of interdependence and dependence, and that international relations are no longer driven primarily by rules or consensus.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Where there was once economic integration, there is now fragmentation and weaponisation of interdependence and dependence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We are now in a world where international relations are no longer driven primarily by rules or by attempts to achieve consensus.

sections.label: Charting Singapore's own path
sections.summary: This passage states that the only viable option is to continue determining long-term national interests and to exercise agency to chart Singapore's own path.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The third, and in my view, the only viable option for us is to continue to determine our long-term national interests and then exercise our agency to chart our own path.

sections.label: Defence spending for six decades
sections.summary: This passage states that disagreement, coercion and conflict are part of international relations, which is why Singapore has spent between 3% and 6% of GDP on defence for six decades.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Disagreement, coercion and even conflict are part and parcel of the cut-and-thrust of international relations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: This is precisely why we have spent between 3% and 6% of our GDP for six decades for defence.

sections.label: Singapore national interests
sections.summary: The passage lists four national interests: sovereignty and unity, essential supplies and navigation, a trusted global hub role, and rules-based multilateralism.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: First, to safeguard our sovereignty, our independence and our national unity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Second, to secure access to essential supplies and the freedom of navigation necessary for us to continue to have access to these essential supplies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The third national interest is to continue to strengthen our role as a trusted global hub for trade, for finance, for wealth management, advanced manufacturing and other global services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The fourth aspect of our national interest is to support a rules-based multilateral approach wherever possible, recognising that challenges to the global commons, like climate change, like pandemics, in fact, have to be tackled collectively because they go beyond the ability of any single country, even a super power, to resolve.

sections.label: Humanitarian aid to Gaza
sections.summary: Singapore has sent 11 tranches of humanitarian aid worth over $25 million to Gaza civilians, aided by diplomatic ties across the Middle East.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Coming back to Gaza, we have and we will do more to alleviate the suffering in Gaza, and in fact we have been able to do more precisely because we have got extensive diplomatic ties across the entire Middle East, and we are one of the few countries, and those of you who travel with me will know, with remarkable access to all sides.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We have sent 11 tranches of humanitarian aid amounting to more than $25 million to help the civilians in Gaza so far, and you know that these fundraising efforts are continuing.

sections.label: MFA political visits
sections.summary: Last year, MFA facilitated over 180 incoming and outgoing political-level visits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Last year, MFA facilitated over 180 visits, incoming and outgoing, at the political level.

sections.label: US largest foreign investor
sections.summary: The US has long been and remains Singapore's largest foreign investor by a long way.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
